kind: assumed inputs and analysis choices; nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository

rounding.note: Decimals kept in results.json. Coarse on purpose: a last-bit difference between C libraries must not change a stored digit.

families.note: All three are distributions on the integers x >= x_min, so their likelihoods are comparable. The lognormal is fitted for x_min = 1 only.
families.power_law: discrete power law (zeta distribution): p(x) = x^-alpha / zeta(alpha, x_min), with zeta(alpha, x_min) = sum over k >= 0 of (x_min + k)^-alpha
families.exponential: discrete exponential (geometric): p(x) = (1 - q) q^(x - x_min); maximum likelihood gives q = m / (m + 1), m the mean excess over x_min
families.lognormal: a lognormal variable rounded up to the next integer: p(x) = Phi((ln x - mu) / sigma) - Phi((ln(x - 1) - mu) / sigma), x >= 1

power_law_fit.primary_x_min_reason: keeps every positive count; zeros are set aside because no power law gives a probability to zero
power_law_fit.x_min_candidates: every distinct positive observed count that leaves at least min_tail_listed values
power_law_fit.tail_cut_rule: among the listed cuts that keep at least min_tail_for_tail_cut values, the one with the smallest Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance to the fitted power law

decisive_p_value_note: Convention of Clauset, Shalizi and Newman (2009): the sign of a log-likelihood ratio is trusted when the p-value of the normalised ratio is below 0.1, and a power law is ruled out when its goodness-of-fit p-value is at most 0.1.

bootstrap.note: Nonparametric: draw 18 values with replacement from the 18 recorded counts, apply the cut, refit the discrete exponent.

simulation_all_positive.note: Synthetic samples of 16 positive counts (the number of positive recorded counts). Each generator uses the parameter fitted to the 16 recorded positive counts, rounded to 2 decimals (the exponential keeps the exact mean 414/16). The script checks that the fitted values round to these.

simulation_tail.note: Synthetic tails above the tail cut (x_min = 13). Each generator uses the parameter fitted to the 12 recorded counts of 13 or more (alpha rounded to 2 decimals; the exponential keeps the exact mean 396/12). Sample size 12 is the observed tail; the larger sizes show what more data would buy.

goodness_of_fit_before_git_grep.note: Synthetic power-law samples for the goodness-of-fit test of the hand-typed counts of the last run before git grep: 16 positive values, x_min = 1, exponent fitted to those counts and rounded to 2 decimals (the script checks it). Same procedure as for the recorded counts.

sampler_checks.note: Draws used only to check the three samplers against their probability formulas.

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical plugin registry for the learner task. Not Streeling data. Answers use the continuous closed forms, which a learner can compute by hand; the discrete fits of the lesson are stored next to them for comparison.
